guide.title: West Hartford, Connecticut: From West Division to Webster's Birthplace
guide.intro: West Hartford began in 1672 as the "West Division" of Hartford, a name that stuck until 1806, when the Connecticut General Assembly began calling it the Society of West Hartford; area residents petitioned for separate incorporation in 1854, and West Hartford became its own town on May 3 of that year. Lexicographer Noah Webster, creator of the first American dictionary, was born here in 1758; his birthplace survives as the Noah Webster House museum on South Main Street. In 1817, the American School for the Deaf opened on North Main Street as the first permanent school for the deaf in the United States, and it still teaches deaf and hard-of-hearing students today. Originally farmland, West Hartford grew mills, tanneries, and blacksmith shops into a thriving industrial area by the late nineteenth century, before becoming an educational hub home to the University of Hartford and the University of Saint Joseph.

sections.heading: From West Division to college town
sections.body: In 1672, the Proprietors of Hartford ordered a Division created to the west, and 'West Division' remained the area's official name until 1806, when the Connecticut General Assembly began calling it the Society of West Hartford; area delegates petitioned for a separate town, and it incorporated on May 3, 1854. Lexicographer Noah Webster was born here in 1758, and his birthplace survives as the Noah Webster House on South Main Street. In 1817, the American School for the Deaf opened on North Main Street as the first permanent school for the deaf in the United States and still serves students today. An early farming area, West Hartford had mills, tanneries, and blacksmith shops, and was a thriving industrial area by the late nineteenth century before turning into an educational hub home to the University of Hartford and the University of Saint Joseph.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: West Hartford is a drive-first destination, reached via I-84, which passes through town, and US Routes 6 and 44, plus CT Routes 4 and 218. There is no rail station in West Hartford itself; the nearest CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak stop is Hartford Union Station in adjacent Hartford. CTfastrak bus rapid transit serves the town at its Elmwood and Flatbush Avenue stations, connecting to downtown Hartford and New Britain; a Flatbush Avenue rail station has secured funding but remains unbuilt.

sections.heading: Blue Back Square and Westmoor Park
sections.body: West Hartford Center and the adjoining Blue Back Square anchor the town's shopping and dining, built around Max's Oyster Bar, Hartford Baking Company, and a run of independent storefronts. Westmoor Park, a 162-acre town-run environmental and agricultural education center, keeps a working demonstration farm with cows, llamas, goats, sheep, donkeys, and poultry alongside wildflower meadows and woodland trails; it earned Level II Arboretum accreditation in 2024. Playhouse on Park, on Park Road, is Greater Hartford's intimate professional theater, with no seat more than four rows from the stage. For a place to stay, the Delamar West Hartford sits right on Blue Back Square, Connecticut's only hotel named to Travel + Leisure's 2026 T+L 500.

faq.question: How do I get to West Hartford?
faq.answer: Drivers use I-84, US Routes 6 and 44, and CT Routes 4 and 218. There's no rail station in town; the nearest CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak stop is Hartford Union Station. CTfastrak buses connect West Hartford's Elmwood and Flatbush Avenue stations to Hartford and New Britain.

faq.question: What is West Hartford's connection to Noah Webster?
faq.answer: Noah Webster, creator of the first American dictionary, was born in West Hartford in 1758. His birthplace survives as the Noah Webster House & West Hartford History Center on South Main Street.

faq.question: What is the American School for the Deaf?
faq.answer: Founded in 1817 on North Main Street, it was the first permanent school for the deaf in the United States and still serves deaf and hard-of-hearing students today.

faq.question: Where should I eat and drink in West Hartford?
faq.answer: New Park Brewing pours house IPAs and sour ales with sourdough pizza; Max's Oyster Bar is the West Hartford Center raw-bar institution; Hartford Baking Company serves scratch-made breads and pastries daily from 7 a.m.

faq.question: Where can I stay in West Hartford?
faq.answer: The Delamar West Hartford, a LEED Gold boutique hotel adjacent to Blue Back Square, is the town's marquee option, with an on-site spa and Artisan Restaurant.

places.name: Noah Webster House & West Hartford History Center
places.address: 227 South Main St, West Hartford, CT 06107
places.summary: Birthplace museum of lexicographer Noah Webster, creator of the first American dictionary, born here in 1758; houses the Tracey M. Wilson West Hartford History Center with exhibits on local history. School-year hours Mon-Fri 1-4 p.m.; summer hours Mon-Sat 10 a.m.-2 p.m.

places.name: Westmoor Park
places.summary: A 162-acre town-run environmental, agricultural, and horticultural education center with a demonstration farm — cows, llamas, goats, sheep, donkeys, and poultry — plus wildflower meadows, gardens, and woodland trails. Trails open daily 7 a.m. to dusk; the farm is open 9 a.m.-4 p.m. Achieved Level II Arboretum accreditation in 2024.

places.name: Playhouse on Park
places.summary: Greater Hartford's intimate professional theater — no seat more than four rows from the stage — staging mainstage plays and musicals, Theatre for Young Audiences shows, and comedy nights, with a pre-K-through-high-school theatre academy.

places.name: New Park Brewing
places.address: 485 New Park Ave, West Hartford, CT 06110
places.summary: Craft brewery founded in 2015, known for IPAs and sour ales, with a taproom serving hand-tossed sourdough pizzas and wings plus The Green Room live-music venue.

places.name: Max's Oyster Bar
places.summary: A West Hartford Center seafood institution from the Max Restaurant Group, with a raw bar of bi-coastal oysters and shellfish alongside chop-house selections. Open daily.

places.name: Hartford Baking Company (West Hartford Center)
places.summary: Artisan bakery-cafe in West Hartford Center serving hand-crafted breads, pastries, coffee, and sandwiches made from scratch daily, open seven days a week from 7 a.m.

places.name: Delamar West Hartford
places.summary: Luxury boutique hotel adjacent to Blue Back Square, built to LEED Gold standard, with an on-site spa, Artisan Restaurant, complimentary breakfast, and valet parking — Connecticut's only property named to Travel + Leisure's T+L 500 for 2026.
